record.paper_title: Open problems on graph eigenvalues studied with AutoGraphiX
record.context_brief: Maximum energy of bicyclic molecular graphs
record.original_question: For n = 14 and for every n at least 16, is the bicyclic molecular graph of order n with maximum energy equal to P_n^{6;6}, where a molecular graph means a connected graph of maximum degree at most 4 and P_n^{6;6} is the graph formed from two 6-cycles and a path P(n−12) by joining one endpoint of the path to one cycle and the other endpoint to the other cycle by single edges?

evidence.page: Energy of a graph, HTML lines 1301-1305
evidence.quote: The problem of finding bicyclic graphs with maximum energy was also widely studied... they conjectured the following... recall that a molecular graph is a connected graph with maximum degree at most 4. Conjecture 5.9... For n = 14 and n ≥ 16, the bicyclic molecular graph of order n with maximal energy is ... represented by the graph P_n^{6;6} obtained from two copies of the cycle C_6 and a path P_{n-12} by attaching with an edge each endpoint of the path to one cycle.

evidence.page: Energy of a graph, HTML lines 1307-1311
evidence.quote: Li and Zhang (2007) gave a partial solution to the conjecture in the case of bipartite bicyclic graphs. The complete solution, in that case, was given by Huo et al. (2011). Theorem 5.10... Let G be any connected, bipartite bicyclic graph on n ≥ 12 vertices. Then E(G) ≤ E(P_n^{6;6}) with equality if and only if G ≡ P_n^{6;6}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A molecular graph is a connected simple graph in which every vertex has degree at most 4. A bicyclic graph is a connected simple graph with exactly n edges on n vertices (equivalently, a connected graph with cyclomatic number 2). The energy E(G) of a graph G is defined as the sum of the absolute values of the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix.

For an integer n ≥ 13, let P_n^{6;6} denote the graph obtained as follows: take two vertex-disjoint copies of the 6-cycle C_6 and a path P_{n−12} on n−12 vertices, then join one endpoint of the path by a single edge to a vertex of the first C_6 and the other endpoint of the path by a single edge to a vertex of the second C_6. (For n = 14, this construction is interpreted with the path P_2 having two endpoints, and for n = 13 with a single vertex serving as the path P_1, but here we consider n = 14 and n ≥ 16.)

Prove or disprove: for n = 14 and for every integer n ≥ 16, among all bicyclic molecular graphs on n vertices, the graph P_n^{6;6} is the unique one attaining the maximum energy E(G).
artifact.status_search_result: The bipartite case of the conjecture was fully resolved by Huo, Ji, Li and Shi (2011), and further partial progress has been made for several classes of non-bipartite bicyclic graphs (e.g., bicyclic graphs containing one even and one odd cycle, and bicyclic graphs containing two odd cycles with one common vertex, the latter settled in 2024). The full conjecture for general (not necessarily bipartite) bicyclic molecular graphs remains open.

status_evidence.title: Solution to a conjecture on the maximal energy of bipartite bicyclic graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Complete solution in the bipartite bicyclic case showing E(G) ≤ E(P_n^{6;6}).
status_evidence.claim: Bipartite case of the conjecture is solved.

status_evidence.title: Maximum energy bicyclic graphs containing two odd cycles with one common vertex
status_evidence.snippet: Proves the conjecture for bicyclic graphs with two odd cycles sharing a common vertex.
status_evidence.claim: Additional partial cases have been resolved; the general conjecture is still open.
